verifier_note: Every factual check below was executed against the read-only snapshot; scratch in /home/rohit/t13scratch. The decisive new method for this theme was to stop arguing about C-route and COMPUTE it: /home/rohit/t13scratch/cdg.py builds the channel-dependency graph directly from the compiler's own generate_routing_tables() output and searches it for cycles, and cdg_suite.py runs that over all 40 rows of benchmarks/instances.csv. Two more computed emulations settle items no reviewer could settle from reading: ftroute2.py rebuilds the graph the RTL actually installs (after out-of-range adjacency writes are discarded) and routes every emitted table through it, and maxp.py emulates the 12-bit adjacency truncation for maxp_mod_fat exactly as noc_system.sv would apply it. T01's watchdog result and T03's scoreboard-gate semantics are treated as settled input and cited, not re-derived.

verdicts.finding: The VC-escape deadlock-freedom discipline described in Sec.4.9 does not exist: every injected packet is hardwired to VC0.
verdicts.observed: THE FINDING IS TRUE AND IT UNDERSTATES. (1) rtl/btree_fsm_fast.sv:629 is the only packet-forming assignment in the design (grep -n 'txf_data' rtl/*.sv returns btree_fsm_fast.sv:387,399,605,629 and nothing else): fsm_txf_data = {ex_addr_b, ex_dest[9:0], 6'b0, ex_data_a}. Bits [69:64] are the literal 6'b0, so the VC-select bit [64] read at rtl/noc_router.sv:118 is always 0 and ibuf_wen[p][1] never asserts. (2) No VC anywhere in the compiler: grep -rniE 'virtual channel|\bvc[0-9_]|escape|dateline|wrap' over src/*.py returns one unrelated hit in sprs_tournament.py:69; grep -cE 'virtual|escape|dateline' src/sprs_core.py = 0. (3) NEW, WORSE #1: the router could not implement a VC-escape discipline even if bit 64 were set. rtl/noc_router.sv:142-143 states in its own comment 'per-port egress FIFOs ... (single FIFO per port, shared across VCs -- VCs are input-side only)' and :154-165 instantiates ONE sync_fifo per port. A shared egress buffer couples the two VCs and destroys the escape-channel property by construction. (4) NEW, WORSE #2: the routing is not dimension-ordered. src/sprs_core.py:667-686 generate_routing_tables is greedy first-strictly-better minimal-distance over adjacency insertion order; there is no dimension ordering anywhere in the file. (5) NEW, WORSE #3 AND DECISIVE: I built the CDG from the emitted tables and it is CYCLIC on 8 of the 35 suite instances small enough to compute, plus both large tori by direct check of torus G=1024 (cycle length 32): med_mod_ring, large_mod_ring, vlarge_mod_ring, vlarge2_mod_ring (cycle length = G, i.e. the textbook bidirectional-ring cycle), large_unbal_torus (6), vlarge_dense_2d (8), med_full_torus and vlarge2_dense_2d (11), max_bal_2d and maxp_bal_2d. Linear, mesh, hypercube and fat-tree are ACYCLIC at every suite size. (6) The verification the paper cites does not exist: main.tex:1540 cites 'a 30-line Python check (validate_routing.py)'; grep -rn validate_routing over the entire snapshot returns 0 hits and the name is absent from MANIFEST.json.
verdicts.what_is_true: Sec.4.9's sentence -- 'the compiler emits routing tables that satisfy a dimension-ordered (DOR) restriction with a VC-escape discipline: packets route dimension-by-dimension, and packets crossing a wrap-around edge use VC1 ... This discharges C-route: the channel-dependency graph on the emitted routing tables is acyclic, and a 30-line Python check (validate_routing.py) verifies acyclicity for every compiled instance' -- is false in every one of its five clauses. Not DOR; no packet uses VC1; the CDG is not acyclic; C-route is not discharged; the checker is not in the artifact. The companion is materially more honest than the paper here (companion/main.tex:258-263 concedes 'a compiler bug can construct a cyclic channel dependency the hardware will faithfully deadlock on. The watchdog converts that into a fail-stop'), so the two documents disagree and the companion has the defensible version.
verdicts.consequence: Single most consequential item in T13. This is NOT repairable by an edit that preserves the claim, because the claim is computably false and a referee with the artifact can run the twenty lines I ran. The cheapest adequate fix is still claim removal, not an RTL or compiler change: restate C-route as an assumption the compiler does NOT establish, adopt the companion's sentence verbatim into the paper, and delete the validate_routing.py citation. Doing that also lets Sec.4.9 lose the DOR/VC1 sentence entirely (about 8 lines) and Fig.4's 11-line value-agnosticism paragraph shrink to one sentence (see T13-X4), so the honest version is SHORTER. Adding a VC field to the ISA plus compiler VC assignment plus a per-VC egress FIFO is a multi-week RTL change that would invalidate all 2,822 cycle counts; it must not be attempted for this paper.

verdicts.finding: fp64_add.sv is not round-to-nearest-even on effective subtraction: systematic 1-ulp error, and the campaign never exercises that path.
verdicts.observed: Re-derived independently of the orchestrator's transcription, using the ARTIFACT'S OWN oracle rather than a re-transcription (/home/rohit/t13scratch/fpchk.py compares sprs_core._fp64_add_bits against exact Fraction arithmetic rounded by Python's correctly-rounded float()). Error rate versus |exponent difference|, 4,000 trials each: 0 -> 0.0%, 1 -> 0.0%, 2 -> 25.3%, 3 -> 38.2%, 5 -> 46.8%, 10 -> 51.2%, 30 -> 49.0%, 52 -> 52.3%, 53 -> 100.0%, 54 -> 0.0%, 60 -> 0.0%. Same-sign control: 0 errors in 4,000. Every error is exactly +1 in the fraction field. This reproduces the orchestrator's table to within sampling noise and confirms the mechanism at rtl/fp64_add.sv:149 ('m_sum = {1'b0, m_big} - {1'b0, m_aligned};' with no borrow of the alignment tail held in sticky at :137) and :226 ('if (guard && (sticky || frac_out[0]))', the ADDITION rounding rule). Unreachability confirmed at src/sprs_core.py:5366-5368: fv = (idx+1)*1000.0 + ((idx*37+13) % 100)/100.0 + 0.007 is strictly positive for every idx, so s_a == s_b on every FADD in all 2,822 runs. ONE CORRECTION TO THE CARRIED-FORWARD SUMMARY: the subtraction is at fp64_add.sv:149, not :146 (the reviewer's :149 is right, the orchestrator's :146 is a typo). ONE ADDITION THE ORCHESTRATOR DID NOT DRAW: because I used the shipped oracle and not a transcription, this also proves the oracle inherits the defect, which means main.tex:3084-3086's 'Python bit-exact FADD mirror ... identical output to RTL on ~10^6 randomised inputs' is true and evidentially worthless -- agreement between two copies of the same wrong algorithm.
verdicts.what_is_true: Exactly the orchestrator's statement, with the line number corrected: effective subtraction is +1 ulp for roughly half of operand pairs whose exponents differ by 5 to 52 binades and for every pair differing by exactly 53; correct at differences 0, 1 and >=54; never wrong on same-sign addition. Structurally unreachable by the campaign, trivially reachable by any real user. No reported number changes.
verdicts.consequence: MUST DISCLOSE, and the disclosure is cheap. Sec.3.6 currently enumerates exactly three IEEE deviations; add a fourth with one sentence naming the reachability asymmetry, and add one clause to app:repro saying the oracle is a mirror of the RTL and therefore cannot certify IEEE conformance. Fixing the RTL is small but would require re-running the FADD equivalence evidence and is not needed for any claim in this paper, because Claim 1 is about agreement, not accuracy.

verdicts.finding: CN-to-NI flow control is mis-sized in every simulated configuration: 16 credits against an 8-deep injection FIFO, with silent packet drop when it fills.
verdicts.observed: MECHANISM CONFIRMED EXACTLY. src/sprs_core.py:5430 emits '.RTR_BUF_DEPTH(16),.NI_BUF_DEPTH(8)'; rtl/noc_system.sv:150-151 passes RTR_BUF_DEPTH into btree_fsm_fast as both TX_BUF_DEPTH and RX_BUF_DEPTH, so the CN's link_tx initialises credits <= 16 (link_tx.sv:29); its receiver is the NI injection FIFO at DEPTH = BUF_DEPTH = NI_BUF_DEPTH = 8 (noc_ni.sv:98); the NI accepts only with room (noc_ni.sv:106) and returns credit only on acceptance (:111-112), while the CN has already popped (btree_fsm_fast.sv:234). THE CONSEQUENCE IS NARROWER IN THREE WAYS, AND ONE OF THEM IS DECISIVE. (a) A DROPPED PACKET CANNOT PRODUCE A WRONG ANSWER, ONLY A HANG. Every SEND carries a partial result to a DMEM address whose scoreboard bit gates the receiver's dependent COMPUTE (btree_fsm_fast.sv:515-521, semantics settled in T03). A dropped packet leaves that bit clear forever, so DE stalls, the watchdog fires at WATCHDOG_MAX = 20,000 consecutive non-retiring cycles, and the run is Pass=False. Therefore ZERO drops occurred in any of the 2,822 passing runs -- this argument costs nothing and completely voids the reviewer's downstream 'all cycle counts' and 'prop:2'. (b) The two-CN-links race is unreachable. noc_ni.sv:80-90 admits exactly one link per cycle, so if both links presented a packet the loser would be destroyed outright -- but every SEND uses link 0: ScheduledOp.link defaults to 0 (sprs_core.py:926), the send_op at sprs_core.py:5199-5204 never passes link=, and encode_send's default is link=0 (sprs_core.py:912). I checked the emitted programs directly across 18 S2 algorithms on five instances (/home/rohit/t13scratch/sends2.py): 0 SEND instructions with a non-zero aux link field, on every program. (c) Reaching the FIFO-full drop needs sustained congestion. Max consecutive SEND instructions in any emitted program across those same 90 compilations is 3 (max total SENDs on one PE reaches 120, at G=32 hypercube and G=128 fat-tree), so a drop needs the router to withhold all 8 of the NI's credits across at least three separate bursts.
verdicts.what_is_true: The mis-sizing is real, it is introduced by the testbench emitter rather than the RTL default, and it applies to every reported run. The drop is unflagged at the point of loss. But it is fail-stop, not silent-wrong, it provably did not happen in any passing run, and the CN-link race that would make it easy is dead code. It survives as a candidate explanation for some of the 21 watchdog fail-stops T01 identified, which T01 could not attribute to a cause.
verdicts.consequence: CLARIFY LIMITATION, not CHANGE IMPLEMENTATION. Two sentences in Sec.4.9 or L-items: the emitted testbenches over-credit the CN-to-NI link (16 credits, 8-entry FIFO), an overflow would drop a packet without a flag, and by the scoreboard argument such a drop can only produce a watchdog fail-stop, never a wrong root -- which is why no passing run can contain one. Rejecting the reviewer's 're-run at least the instances that timed out': re-running is the most expensive option, it cannot distinguish this cause from the others without an added monitor, and the claim it would defend (no wrong root) is already established for free.

verdicts.finding: The single unvalidated instance is structurally unbuildable, not merely expensive: 4,192 routers exceed the 12-bit adjacency interface and the stated MAX_ROUTERS.
verdicts.observed: THE FACTS ARE RIGHT AND THE WORD 'UNBUILDABLE' IS WRONG, IN A WAY THAT MAKES THE FINDING STRONGER, NOT WEAKER. Facts: build_topology('fat_tree',4096) gives n_routers = 4192 with ports_per_router = 66 (recomputed, matches \RadixMaxRouters = 4,192); rtl/noc_system.sv:67-70 declares adj_rtr_id/adj_port_id/adj_target_rtr/adj_target_port as [11:0] and src/sprs_core.py:5419,5447-5448 emits 'adj_rtr_id=r[11:0] ... adj_target_rtr=tr[11:0]'; I counted the adjacency table for that instance: 12,288 entries, ALL 12,288 of which touch a router id >= 4096 (96 routers are out of range). noc_system.sv:278 does use 12'hFFF as the disconnected sentinel, which collides with router 4095. Nothing enforces MAX_ROUTERS: grep shows noc_pkg.sv:13 is its only occurrence in the entire design. BUT THE TESTBENCH WOULD ELABORATE AND RUN -- an out-of-range unpacked-array write is a no-op, not an error, and noc_system.sv:281 explicitly guards the wiring with 'if (tr < N_ROUTERS && tp < PORTS_PER_RTR)'. So I emulated the configuration the RTL would actually end up with (/home/rohit/t13scratch/maxp.py, applying the 12-bit truncation, the out-of-range-port write drop, and the 12'hFFF sentinel exactly as the RTL does). Result: 8,223 links installed, of which ZERO match the intended topology; 1,984 adjacency writes discarded for port >= 66; and routing 900 random leaf-to-leaf pairs with the emitted routing tables gives 0 delivered and 900 non-terminating. The same 900 pairs on the untruncated fabric give 900 delivered, 0 dead, 0 loops.
verdicts.what_is_true: maxp_mod_fat is buildable and elaborable; what it is not is CORRECT. The emitted testbench configures a network with no relation to the intended fat-tree, in which no packet can reach its destination, so the run could not have settled with unlimited wall-clock. L0's 'This is a resource limit, not a negative result' is therefore false as an explanation. The 12-bit field is the root cause, and it is a hard ceiling at 4,095 routers, not 4,096 (the sentinel takes one).
verdicts.consequence: CLARIFY LIMITATION, zero page cost, and the honest version is more informative than the current one. Replace L0's resource explanation with: 'maxp_mod_fat instantiates 4,192 routers, but the testbench's adjacency-configuration interface carries a 12-bit router id (noc_system.sv:67-70), so the 96 routers above 4,095 alias onto routers 0..95 and the emitted configuration does not describe the intended topology. The instance is excluded for that reason, not for wall-clock; the 58.9 core-hours spent on it were spent on an unbuildable configuration.' Keep the existing true sentence that the software oracle agrees on the N=8192 root. Do NOT widen the field and re-attempt: five attempts already cost 58.9 core-hours before the field was even the binding problem, and the instance adds nothing to Claim 1 that the two other N=8192 points do not already give.

verdicts.finding: The one instance that never validated emits 4,192 routers and has every adjacency write truncated to 12 bits; the paper attributes its absence solely to simulator resources.
verdicts.observed: Same evidence as D069, independently recomputed: n_routers = 4192; 12,288 adjacency entries; 12,288 of them touch a router >= 4096. The reviewer's counts reproduce to the digit. This issue and D069 are one issue seen from the compiler view and the RTL view; the RTL view (D069) is the more complete of the two and should absorb this one.
verdicts.what_is_true: Identical in substance to D069.
verdicts.consequence: Merge into D069. One decision, one edit to L0.

verdicts.finding: Every fat-tree instance with G>=12 emits adjacency port indices beyond the declared PORTS_PER_RTR, and the routing tables use only one core switch.
verdicts.observed: COUNTS CONFIRMED, CONSEQUENCE REFUTED. Recomputed over the suite (/home/rohit/t13scratch/ft.py): out-of-range adjacency entries are G=12 ppr=6 maxport=6 (3 entries); G=32 ppr=8 maxport=9 (12); G=64 ppr=10 maxport=12 (24); G=128 ppr=14 maxport=18 (55); G=256 ppr=18 maxport=24 (112); G=2048 ppr=48 maxport=69 (990); G=4096 ppr=66 maxport=96 (1,984). Zero out-of-range on linear, ring, mesh, torus or hypercube at any size. The reviewer's five figures reproduce exactly. THEN I CHECKED WHAT IT COSTS (/home/rohit/t13scratch/ftroute2.py). The RTL discards those writes (out-of-range unpacked-array write at noc_system.sv:99 is a no-op; the wiring loop at :281 guards on tp < PORTS_PER_RTR), so I rebuilt the graph the fabric actually installs and asked whether ANY routing-table entry on a REACHABLE router points at a port that graph does not wire: the answer is 0 at G=12, 32, 64, 128, 256 and 2048. I then routed 132 to 1,599 random leaf-to-leaf pairs per instance through the installed graph using the emitted tables: 0 dead ports, 0 non-terminating paths, at every size. Only the surplus core switches are orphaned (G=2048: 2,094 of 2,116 routers remain reachable). AND THE RADIX CLAIM SURVIVES INTACT: I computed the maximum number of WIRED ports on any router for every instance (/home/rohit/t13scratch/radix.py) and it equals PORTS_PER_RTR at 100% on every topology at every size, so Table I's radix and Table II's O(P^2) crossbar price real ports, not phantom ones.
verdicts.what_is_true: The emitter does produce port indices the fabric silently discards, and the elaborated fat-tree has exactly ONE core switch instead of k/2 at every G>=12. It is nevertheless a correctly-routed, fully-connected network on which every emitted route is valid -- which is why those instances passed. The only quantity that moves is bisection bandwidth, and it moves in the paper's DISFAVOUR: Topology._bbc min-cuts over the full edge set including the discarded links, and compute_lower_bound divides cross-cut traffic by that bandwidth (sprs_core.py:1219-1230), so an over-estimated bisection makes Omega SMALLER and the reported ratio-to-Omega LARGER. The paper's fat-tree Omega ratios are conservative, not flattering.
verdicts.consequence: REMOVE OR NARROW, one sentence, best placed in the companion. 'For k >= 4 the fat-tree emitter assigns pod-to-core ports above the declared radix, so the elaborated fabric uses a single core switch; every emitted route is valid on that fabric, and the surplus cores carry no traffic.' Reject ADD ANALYSIS (the reviewer's proposed action): the analysis is done here and its outcome is one clause. Reject any re-emit-and-re-run: the root value is topology-independent by Proposition 1 and 2,822 runs already passed on this fabric.

verdicts.finding: The credit-return counter is described as a per-cycle tally but is an accumulating backlog that overflows at 4.
verdicts.observed: MECHANISM CONFIRMED. rtl/noc_router.sv:192 declares credit_pending at $clog2(NUM_VCS+1) = 2 bits; :210 does 'credit_pending[p] <= credit_pending[p] + new_reads - 1' -- an accumulator, not a tally. Hand-traced with sustained new_reads=2: 1, 2, 3, then 3+2-1 = 4 truncates to 0, losing four credits monotonically. The arbiter does permit new_reads=2: noc_router.sv:284-293 guards only '!v_ibuf_ren[cand_port][cand_vc]', so (p,0) and (p,1) can both win in one cycle to different output ports. UNREACHABLE IN EVERY REPORTED RUN, FOR EXACTLY D065'S REASON: with packet bit 64 hardwired to 0, ibuf_wen[p][1] never asserts, so ibuf_rrdy[p][1] is never high, so new_reads is in {0,1} in every cycle of every one of the 2,822 runs and credit_pending is provably always 0.
verdicts.what_is_true: The RTL does not do what main.tex:1527-1531 says it does, and the register would overflow at NUM_VCS=2 under double reads. Zero of the campaign's cycles can exercise it. D065 and D070 are one finding: the dead VC1 simultaneously voids the deadlock argument and masks the counter overflow.
verdicts.consequence: REMOVE OR NARROW. Correct the register's description in Sec.4.9 (it is a pending-credit backlog drained one per cycle, not a per-cycle tally), and correct the L-item 'Credit-pulse counter width', whose current sentence 'An SVA check bounds the counter' cannot be supported -- the SVA file is not in the artifact (see T13-X2). Bundle with D065 so the two are decided together.

verdicts.finding: The resource table prices router FIFOs at depth 8; every simulated instance instantiates depth 16.
verdicts.observed: src/sprs_core.py:5430 emits '.RTR_BUF_DEPTH(16)'; rtl/noc_system.sv:235 passes it as the router's BUF_DEPTH, which sizes both the per-VC ingress FIFOs (noc_router.sv:91) and the egress FIFO (noc_router.sv:156); sync_fifo.sv:25 allocates DEPTH x WIDTH bits. I recomputed every cell of paper/tables/resource.tex from its own stated formula: at depth 8 I reproduce 26,208 / 53,344 / 598,912 exactly, so the table is internally consistent and this is one wrong input, not an arithmetic error. At depth 16 the subtotals become 37,728 / 78,688 / 750,976 -- the reviewer's three figures to the digit -- and all four derived macros move: \RouterBlowup 22.85 (23) -> 19.91 (20), \XbarShareFt 69.8% -> 55.7%, \AggLoMbit 102.4 -> 147.4, \AggFtMbit 2394.3 -> 3002.3.
verdicts.what_is_true: The table is right for the RTL default (noc_system.sv:27, BUF_DEPTH = 8) and wrong for the parameterisation every reported run used. The sharpest way to put it is that main.tex:1600 says 'We report the flat figure because it is what we simulated' and on this one input that sentence is exactly backwards. The companion repeats the error at companion/main.tex:295-296 ('TX and RX buffers 8 entries').
verdicts.consequence: EDIT, zero page cost, and the direction is mixed rather than bad: the fat-tree/mesh blowup weakens from 23x to 20x, but the aggregate rises from 2,394 to 3,002 Mbit, which strengthens the paragraph's actual conclusion that a flat crossbar is the wrong structure at that radix. Cheapest form: regenerate tables/resource.tex and data/resource_macros.tex at depth 16 (the script paper/scripts/gen_resource.py already exists). Acceptable alternative at zero risk: leave the table and add to its caption 'at the RTL default BUF_DEPTH = 8; the campaign's testbenches instantiate 16, raising the P=66 subtotal to 750,976 bits.'

verdicts.finding: The 512-entry IMEM budget is neither enforced nor used to reject: the emitted testbench sizes IMEM to fit the program, and the 278 'rejected' compilations were marked feasible.
verdicts.observed: Recomputed over all 40 results/results/*/sw_results.csv (/home/rohit/t13scratch/imem.py, 7,200 rows). error_code histogram {E_OK 6499, E_BYPASSED 390, E_IMEM_OF 278, E_EVAL_TIMEOUT 33}; valid==True on 6,785 rows; imem_ok==False on 693; and the intersection 'imem_ok False AND valid True' is exactly 278, identical to the count of rows with max_imem > 512. So all 278 E_IMEM_OF rows carry valid=True: they were flagged, not rejected. The emitter's sizing is src/sprs_core.py:5381-5384 'max_imem = max(len(progs[g])...); imem_sz = 1; while imem_sz < max_imem: imem_sz *= 2; imem_sz = max(imem_sz,64)' with '.CN_IMEM({imem_sz})' at :5432, which overrides btree_pkg.sv:19 IMEM_DEPTH = 512. This corroborates T01-X3 independently: 117 of the 2,920 unique-testbench rows are E_IMEM_OF (vlarge_extreme_1d 67, large_extreme_1d 46, max_mod_fat 1, max_bal_2d 1, maxp_bal_2d 1, maxp_mod_fat 1), so 116 were simulated on validated instances. The paper's per-instance breakdown is nonetheless EXACTLY RIGHT: E_IMEM_OF per instance over all 7,200 is large_extreme_1d 120, vlarge_extreme_1d 120, max_mod_fat 10, max_bal_2d 10, maxp_bal_2d 10, maxp_mod_fat 8, total 278 -- matching main.tex:2026-2031's 120/120/10/8 verbatim. DMEM, unlike IMEM, IS fixed: dmem_sz = hw.dmem_depth = 512 (sprs_core.py:361, 5384), so '.CN_DMEM(512)' on every instance.
verdicts.what_is_true: One word in main.tex:2022-2024 is wrong -- 'rejects' -- and everything numerically attached to it is right. The S5 pass flags and the tournament records the flag but nothing filters on it, so 113 of the 278 were RTL-validated with an enlarged IMEM and sit inside the headline 2,822. The paper's own sentence 'they are a property of the 512-entry budget, not of the ABI' remains true.
verdicts.consequence: EDIT plus one clause, and it is nearly free. 'the S5 memory pass flags rather than truncating; 278 of the 7,200 compilations exceeded the budget, and the emitted testbench sizes IMEM to the next power of two above the longest program, so 113 of them were nonetheless RTL-validated at an enlarged IMEM.' This costs one line and closes D061, D148, D181(iii) and T01-X3 at once. Reject CHANGE IMPLEMENTATION (cap CN_IMEM at 512 and re-run): re-running 2,920 testbenches to enforce a budget that constrains nothing about the ABI is the most expensive option available and would remove 113 passing data points.

verdicts.finding: Sec 5.9 measures router radix from the emitted testbenches but assumes a per-PE IMEM depth those same testbenches contradict.
verdicts.observed: Same script and data as D061. Over the 2,920 unique-testbench rows, max_imem ranges 14 to 3,402 and the emitted CN_IMEM distribution is {64: 875, 128: 937, 256: 671, 512: 320, 1024: 113, 2048: 3, 4096: 1}. So only 320 of 2,920 emitted testbenches -- 11% -- instantiate the 512-entry IMEM that main.tex:1609 prices, 2,483 instantiate less and 117 more; the single CN_IMEM(4096) is maxp_mod_fat, which was never simulated, so the largest attempted is 2,048. CORRECTION TO THE REVIEWER'S SUB-NUMBERS: they give 'max_imem ranges from 12 to 1,708, so CN_IMEM spans 64 to 2,048'; the true range over unique-testbench rows is 14 to 3,402 and CN_IMEM spans 64 to 4,096 (64 to 2,048 among those actually simulated). Separately, CN_RT_DEPTH is never overridden by the emitter and defaults to 4096 (noc_system.sv:39), so every router in every instance really does instantiate the 4,096-entry routing table Table II prices -- that row is right, and more right than the paper claims.
verdicts.what_is_true: The juxtaposition the reviewer names is real: Sec 5.9 boasts of measuring PORTS_PER_RTR from the testbenches and then two paragraphs later assumes an IMEM depth those same testbenches contradict 89% of the time. The \PerPEBits = 65,536 figure is therefore an upper bound on almost every instance, not a measurement.
verdicts.consequence: EDIT, one clause, merged with D061's. 'Per-PE memory is topology-independent: DMEM is fixed at 512 x 64, and IMEM is sized per instance to the next power of two above the longest program (64 to 2,048 entries across the suite); we price the 512-entry case.' Zero page cost. Reject the reviewer's request for a distribution table: the range in a clause carries the same information at a tenth of the space.

verdicts.finding: MAX_ROUTERS = 4096 is stated as the fabric ceiling while the suite's largest instance is reported to instantiate 4,192 routers.
verdicts.observed: main.tex:1207 says 'The fabric supports a cluster of up to MAX_ROUTERS = 4096 PEs' -- and read as a PE bound that is satisfied, since maxp_mod_fat has 4,096 PEs. The mismatch is between the parameter's NAME and comment (noc_pkg.sv:13 'MAX_ROUTERS = 4096; // max routers in a system (supports G<=4096)') and the 4,192 routers that same instance instantiates. grep over rtl/*.sv shows MAX_ROUTERS occurs exactly once, its own declaration, so it constrains nothing. The reviewer is also right that the CSV is consistent with a timeout: results/results/live_hw_results_maxp_mod_fat.csv, five rows, all SIM_WALLCLOCK_TIMEOUT_BYPASS.
verdicts.what_is_true: The paper's sentence is defensible as written; what is not defensible is using an unreferenced parameter as if it were an enforced fabric ceiling while a suite instance exceeds the quantity it is named for. The REAL ceiling, established under D069, is 4,095 routers, imposed by the 12-bit adjacency id with 12'hFFF taken as the disconnected sentinel -- and that one is enforced, silently, by truncation.
verdicts.consequence: Fold into D069's L0 edit; do not spend a separate sentence. The honest replacement names the binding constraint: 'the adjacency-configuration interface carries a 12-bit router id, so the addressable router range is 0..4,094; MAX_ROUTERS in noc_pkg.sv is vestigial and enforces nothing, as is MAX_PORTS.' The paper already says exactly this about MAX_PORTS at main.tex:1562-1568, so the sentence pattern is in hand and costs one line.

verdicts.finding: Paper describes four DMEM write agents; the RTL has three, and the companion says three.
verdicts.observed: rtl/btree_fsm_fast.sv:365-382 is a three-way priority mux (piu_dmem_wr > gci_dmem_wr > fsm_dmem_wr) and :706-721 sets the scoreboard from exactly those three conditions. GENERATE never drives fsm_dmem_wr: btree_fsm_fast.sv:613-616 only pulses gci_start, so a GENERATE's value is committed by the GCI agent, which is already counted. Module header btree_fsm_fast.sv:22 '3-way DMEM write arbitration: PIU > GCI > FSM'; companion/main.tex:222 'Three agents write DMEM'. The likely source of the paper's four is the RTL's own scoreboard comment at btree_fsm_fast.sv:704, which names four ROLES over three PORTS.
verdicts.what_is_true: Three physical write ports. The paper's parenthetical describing the fourth agent as 'the FSM path that closes a GENERATE' is wrong about which path commits it. F-arb itself, which is about the priority order, is correctly described.
verdicts.consequence: EDIT: 'four' -> 'three' in Sec.4.5, in Fig.5, and in Fig.5's caption; drop the GENERATE bullet. Zero page cost, and it also removes a paper-versus-companion disagreement without touching the companion. It touches main.tex:1200 too ('four independent write agents').

verdicts.finding: piu_misroute is a write-only signal: the misroute drop is real, the flag is unobservable outside the module.
verdicts.observed: grep -rn piu_misroute over rtl/ returns exactly four lines, all in btree_fsm_fast.sv: :256 declaration, :287 and :293 clear, :317 set. No read anywhere, not a module port, not exported by noc_system.sv. The drop and the credit return themselves are correctly implemented at btree_fsm_fast.sv:314-319. The SVA the paper cites to observe it (tb/sva/tb_sva_e2e.sv) does not exist in the artifact -- see T13-X2.
verdicts.what_is_true: Exactly as stated. F-misroute's drop-and-return-credit half is real hardware; its 'asserts piu_misroute' half is an internal signal with no observer anywhere in the artifact, and the assertion cited to observe it is missing too.
verdicts.consequence: EDIT, one clause: say the flag is internal and not exported, and delete the corresponding SVA bullet. Reject the reviewer's CHANGE IMPLEMENTATION (export it): exporting the signal changes no result and there is no run to redo, so it cannot raise acceptance probability.

verdicts.finding: Companion contradicts the paper and the RTL on forwarding depth, and its inventory table is off by five lines.
verdicts.observed: All three sub-claims reproduce. (a) companion/main.tex:232 'One level of write-to-read forwarding'; rtl/btree_fsm_fast.sv:166-181 implements two, with explicit 'Level 1'/'Level 2' comments and dmem_wr_*_d1/_d2 register pairs feeding both read ports -- the paper is right and the companion is copying the stale module header at btree_fsm_fast.sv:17. (b) wc -l over rtl/*.sv and fpga/*.sv: noc_router.sv is 306 lines against the companion's 301 at companion/main.tex:86; every other one of the thirteen rows matches exactly; actual total 2,304 + 1,439 = 3,743 against the claimed 3,738, so the 5-line gap is entirely noc_router. (The README badge 'SystemVerilog 3.7k lines' inherits it.) (c) companion/main.tex:129-133 'there is no way for a program to deadlock waiting on a message that never arrives' contradicts main.tex Sec.4.7 and the scoreboard gate at btree_fsm_fast.sv:515-521, and is falsified by T01's 21 observed watchdog fail-stops. I FOUND THREE MORE COMPANION-VERSUS-RTL MISMATCHES. (d) companion:253-255 'Arbitration is two-level round-robin --- among VCs within a port, then among ports for each output' is not what noc_router.sv:244-296 does: it is a single flattened round-robin over NUM_PORTS x NUM_VCS candidates per output port, with no VC-level stage. (e) companion:295-296 'TX and RX buffers 8 entries' is contradicted by noc_system.sv:150-151 plus sprs_core.py:5430, which make them 16 (same root cause as D071). (f) companion:299-303 'The 512-entry instruction memory is the binding constraint on instance feasibility ... the compiler rejects it rather than emitting a truncated program' is falsified by D061 above and by T01-X3.
verdicts.what_is_true: Six independent companion statements disagree with the RTL or with the main paper. None of them affects a reported number. Note that on the one item that matters most, the companion is MORE honest than the paper: companion:258-263 concedes that a cyclic channel dependency will deadlock the hardware, while main.tex:1538-1541 claims the CDG is verified acyclic.
verdicts.consequence: EDIT the companion; the companion is not billed, so this is six one-line corrections at zero page cost. Item (f) is the one that matters, because it repeats in the companion a claim D061 shows the paper making falsely -- fix both in the same pass so the two documents cannot be caught disagreeing about the same fact in two directions.

verdicts.finding: Reported G values are requested worker counts; the instantiated PE count differs for several suite entries.
verdicts.observed: Recomputed independently of T01 by running build_topology over all 40 rows of benchmarks/instances.csv: exactly 8 instances instantiate more PEs than the tabulated G -- npow2g_small_mesh 5->6 (mesh_3x2), npow2_tiny_hc 7->8 (hypercube_3d), npow2_small_torus 10->12 (torus_4x3), med_dense_mesh 8->9 (mesh_3x3), med_full_torus 128->132 (torus_12x11), large_unbal_torus 32->36 (torus_6x6), vlarge2_dense_2d 128->132 (torus_12x11), maxp_bal_2d 2048->2070 (torus_46x45). Identical to T01's list, from a separate script. T01 additionally corroborated it against the released PerfAllGPUs vector for maxp_bal_2d (2,070 entries) and the '[FAIL] 8192L 2070G torus_46x45' error string, so this is settled twice over. The surplus PEs are loaded with a single NOP (sprs_core.py, 'Load NOP for unused GPUs so they reach DONE').
verdicts.what_is_true: Mesh, torus and hypercube constructors round the worker count up, so the elaborated fabric is larger than the tabulated G on 8 of 40 instances, including the paper's headline reshape example at main.tex:2165-2167 (G=128 torus is a 132-PE torus).
verdicts.consequence: EDIT, one footnote on Table I, essentially zero page cost. T01 already drafted the wording; do not duplicate the decision here -- record T13's role as independent corroboration and let T01's ledger entry own it.

verdicts.finding: Minor spec mismatches: packet reserved-field width, the identity slot's value, and the IMEM budget.
verdicts.observed: (i) CONFIRMED. main.tex:1259 draws 'reserved [69:65] (5b)' with a VC bit at [64]; both package headers document '[69:64] reserved (6 bits) -- future use' (noc_pkg.sv:32, btree_pkg.sv:66) with no VC field. The router's use of bit 64 (noc_router.sv:118) makes the figure correct and the package headers stale. (ii) CONFIRMED BUT ALREADY DISCLOSED, SO NEARLY HARMLESS. btree_fsm_fast.sv:183-186 initialises DMEM to all-zero in an initial block (not on reset) and :709 sets scoreboard[0], so DMEM[0] is the identity for ADD, SADD, FADD, OR and XOR but not for MAX (needs -inf), MIN (+inf) or AND (all-ones). What the reviewer missed is that main.tex:1123-1126 ALREADY says 'The identity slot DMEM[0] is reserved but unused in the present workload', and sprs_tournament.py uses ALU_FADD exclusively (lines 285, 377, 796, 1587), so nothing reads the slot in any reported run. The over-claim is confined to the F-id sentence at main.tex:1314. (iii) CONFIRMED, duplicate of D061/D148.
verdicts.what_is_true: Three real mismatches, all cosmetic. (ii) is the only one with any semantic content and the paper has already hedged it two pages earlier.
verdicts.consequence: EDIT, three clauses, zero page cost. (i) change the two package comments or the figure -- prefer the packages, since the figure is the one the RTL agrees with. (ii) change F-id to 'DMEM[0] is initialised to zero, the identity for ADD/FADD/OR/XOR; MAX, MIN and AND would require a different initialiser' -- this costs six words and pre-empts a referee who checks the extension claim at main.tex:2501. (iii) already covered by the D061 edit.

verdicts.finding: EXTENDED, NOT IN THE DOCKET, AND IT REFUTES THE THEME'S OWN HYPOTHESIS: the missing VC discipline is NOT the cause of the 21 cyclic-topology watchdog timeouts.
verdicts.observed: themes.json T13 states 'the missing VC discipline plus cyclic-topology timeouts may be the same bug', and D065's downstream list names the 21 failures. I computed the CDG for every instance that produced one. T01 established the 21 breakdown as vlarge2_mod_ring x10 (ring, CDG CYCLIC), vlarge_dense_hc x7 (hypercube_5d, CDG ACYCLIC), max_dense_hc and maxp_dense_hc (hypercube, ACYCLIC), max_bal_2d and maxp_bal_2d (torus, CYCLIC), plus a DFSseed cluster that includes max_mod_fat (fat-tree, ACYCLIC). At least 10 of the 21 -- every hypercube and fat-tree failure -- occurred on a topology whose emitted routing tables have a provably acyclic channel-dependency graph, where a routing deadlock is impossible. Conversely, hundreds of OTHER configurations on the same cyclic-CDG ring and torus instances passed. T01 further showed the failures cluster by ALGORITHM (2i CPOP on vlarge2_mod_ring, 2g DSC on vlarge_dense_hc, 2f DFSseed across six instances), not by topology.
verdicts.what_is_true: Cyclic CDG and watchdog timeout are two real, independent facts about this artifact that happen to share a topology vocabulary. The 21 timeouts correlate with the S2 algorithm, not with CDG cyclicity. A referee who reads D065 and T01 together will reach for this inference; the paper should not offer it and the council should not endorse it.
verdicts.consequence: DO NOT COUPLE THEM. Report the cyclic CDG as a correctness-argument defect (C-route is not discharged) and the 21 timeouts as Property-2 outcome (c) evidence, exactly as T01 recommends, and say nothing that ties the two. Coupling them would invite a referee to demand a root-cause analysis of the 21 -- an expensive re-simulation with tracing -- to defend a link the data does not support.

verdicts.finding: EXTENDED: three of the five artifacts the reproducibility appendix names as evidence do not exist in the artifact, and a fourth is at a different path.
verdicts.observed: main.tex:3087-3091 lists 'SVA suite at tb/sva/tb_sva_e2e.sv; Python post-condition pass validate_abi.py plus validate_routing.py' and 'tests/mutation/ contains address-substitution and leaf-corruption harnesses'. find over the whole snapshot: tb_sva_e2e -> 0 hits; validate_abi -> 0 hits; validate_routing -> 0 hits; tests/ -> does not exist (the harness is at experiments/mutation/_mutation_runner.py). None of the three names appears in MANIFEST.json. No file matching tb_*.sv exists anywhere (T01 found the same). These are not incidental: validate_routing.py is cited at main.tex:1539-1541 as the thing that discharges C-route, validate_abi.py at main.tex:1152-1156 as the compile-time post-condition, and tb_sva_e2e.sv at main.tex:1158-1163 as the source of five named runtime assertions plus at :1641 ('An SVA check bounds the counter') and :1544 ('We corroborate dynamically via SVA').
verdicts.what_is_true: Every dynamic-assertion claim in Sec.3.8 and the C-route acyclicity check are unverifiable from the artifact, and the C-route one is additionally false on the data (D065). This is the finding most likely to sink an artifact-evaluated submission, because an AE reviewer runs exactly these paths.
verdicts.consequence: Either ship the three files or remove the citations. Removing is cheaper and safe: delete the tb/sva path and the validate_routing.py clause, replace 'We corroborate dynamically via SVA' with nothing, and change the Sec.3.8 SVA paragraph to describe what the testbench actually checks -- the compile-time EXPECTED comparison at sprs_core.py:5482,5573, which T01 and T07 verified. That is a NEGATIVE page delta. If the files exist outside the snapshot, shipping them is better; but the paper must not cite validate_routing.py at all, because running it would now have to report cycles.

verdicts.finding: EXTENDED: the artifact contains a systematic pattern of dead second channels, and every latent RTL bug in this theme is masked by one of them.
verdicts.observed: Four independent instances, each verified above: (1) VC1 is never entered, because packet bit 64 is a literal 6'b0 at btree_fsm_fast.sv:629 -- this masks the credit_pending overflow (D070). (2) CN link 1 is never used, because every SEND carries aux link 0 (sprs_core.py:912, 926, 5199-5204; 0 non-zero link fields in 90 compiled programs across 18 S2 algorithms) -- this masks the NI's one-winner-per-cycle injection race (noc_ni.sv:80-90), which would destroy a packet outright. (3) In every fat-tree at G>=12, k/2 - 1 core switches carry no traffic (D063). (4) noc_link.sv is compiled (it is in rtl/filelist.f) but never instantiated: grep -rn noc_link over rtl/ and fpga/ returns only its own file, the filelist, and three comments in noc_system.sv (:10, :16, :253) that claim inter-router links go through it. LINK_LATENCY is likewise a dead parameter, as are CN_TX_BUF and CN_RX_BUF (noc_system.sv:32-33, never referenced) and MAX_ROUTERS, MAX_PORTS and MAX_VCS (noc_pkg.sv:13,14,17, each appearing exactly once). btree_pkg.sv:87 declares a SECOND MAX_PORTS with a DIFFERENT value (4 against noc_pkg's 8); both are unreferenced.
verdicts.what_is_true: The design was parameterised for capabilities the campaign never used, and the unused half of each pair is where the defects live. This is the same structural blindness T07 found in the oracle and the fp64 finding found in the leaf generator: the evaluation cannot see a class of defect by construction, because the stimulus never enters the path.
verdicts.consequence: This is the strongest INTERPRETIVE material T13 produces and it is worth about four sentences in the limitations section, because naming it converts a list of errata into a methodological observation a referee will respect: 'the fabric instantiates two VCs, two CN links and k/2 fat-tree core switches; the compiler uses one of each. Every RTL defect we and our reviewers found lies in the unused half, which is the expected consequence of validating a parameterised design at a single point in its parameter space.' It costs almost nothing and it pre-empts the referee who is assembling the same list.

verdicts.finding: EXTENDED, AND IT SAVES PAGES: the paper spends eleven lines defending a value-agnosticism property that the RTL makes trivially true.
verdicts.observed: main.tex:1276-1287 argues at length that VC selection is 'a function of a header bit, not any payload bit', that payload-dependent VC selection would make contention 'adversarially perturbable under value distributions', and that 'header-only VC steering therefore plays a role in the empirical-repeatability argument'. Fig.4's caption (main.tex:1269-1274) repeats it. Since bit [64] is the constant 6'b0 (btree_fsm_fast.sv:629), VC selection is not merely header-dependent, it is CONSTANT, and value-independence is immediate rather than argued.
verdicts.what_is_true: The paper's conclusion is correct and more strongly supported than the paper says. The eleven-line argument is defending the weaker of two available positions.
verdicts.consequence: COMPRESS. Replace the paragraph with one sentence -- 'All packets are injected on VC0, so VC selection is constant and cannot depend on payload; routing latency is value-agnostic by construction' -- and shorten Fig.4's caption to match. Roughly 0.12 billed pages saved, the claim gets stronger, and it lands the D065 disclosure and the D181(i) figure correction in the same edit. This is the rare item that is simultaneously a concession, a strengthening and a page saving.

verdicts.finding: EXTENDED: the fat-tree degeneracy makes the paper's Omega ratios CONSERVATIVE, not flattering.
verdicts.observed: Topology._bbc computes bisection by min-cut over self._edges, which contains all pod-to-core links including the k/2 - 1 per pod the RTL discards (D063). compute_lower_bound then divides cross-cut messages by that bandwidth (sprs_core.py:1219-1230: 'link_time = math.ceil(drain_cycles / bisection_bw)'), so an over-estimated bisection makes lb_bisect smaller, Omega smaller, and the reported ratio makespan/Omega LARGER. I separately verified that hop distances are unaffected: every pod connects to core 0, so the leaf-to-leaf distance is unchanged, which is why all 1,599 sampled routes still deliver in 4 hops.
verdicts.what_is_true: The compiler's fat-tree lower bound is computed against a network with more bisection than the fabric has, which makes the ratio-to-Omega column look worse for fat-trees than it should. This is an understatement in the paper's own evidence.
verdicts.consequence: NO CHANGE, or at most half a clause folded into the D063 sentence ('...and the surplus cores carry no traffic, so the fat-tree Omega ratios are computed against a more capable network than the one simulated'). Recomputing Omega is not worth a page or a risk; the direction of the error is favourable and stating the direction is free.

verdicts.finding: EXTENDED: the radix table and the crossbar term survive scrutiny completely, which is worth knowing before anyone proposes weakening them.
verdicts.observed: The natural inference from D063 -- that PORTS_PER_RTR = 66 prices ports the fabric never wires, so Table I and the O(P^2) crossbar argument are inflated -- is false. I computed, for every (topology, G) in the suite, the maximum number of ports actually WIRED on any router after discarding out-of-range adjacency writes (/home/rohit/t13scratch/radix.py): it equals PORTS_PER_RTR at 100% utilisation on every topology at every size, including fat_tree at G=4096 where a pod router uses ports 0..65 (port 0 local, 1..k to leaves, k+1 to core 0). Table I's span 3-66 reproduces exactly from build_topology. And main.tex:1562-1568's statement that MAX_PORTS 'is declared in noc_pkg.sv but is never referenced by any module' is literally true (grep: one occurrence).
verdicts.what_is_true: Sec.5.9's radix measurement is sound, its honesty about MAX_PORTS is accurate, and the P=66 crossbar cost is real. Only the FIFO depth input (D071) is wrong.
verdicts.consequence: NO CHANGE, and record it so the council does not spend pages defending a table that does not need defending. The one caveat worth adding is btree_pkg.sv:87's second, conflicting MAX_PORTS = 4, which the paper does not mention; one parenthetical ('both packages declare an unreferenced MAX_PORTS, with different values') would close it, but it is optional.

fp64_add_verdict: CARRIED FORWARD AND INDEPENDENTLY RE-DERIVED, WITH ONE CORRECTION AND ONE ADDITION. The orchestrator's finding in T13_fp64_finding.json is correct in every substantive respect and I reproduce its rate table: 0.0% at |exponent difference| 0 and 1, 25.3% at 2, 38.2% at 3, ~47-52% flat across 5..52, 100.0% at exactly 53, 0.0% at >=54, with every error exactly +1 ulp and zero errors on same-sign addition (4,000 trials per bucket, /home/rohit/t13scratch/fpchk.py). CORRECTION: the un-borrowed subtraction is at rtl/fp64_add.sv:149, not :146; the rounding rule is at :226 as stated. ADDITION: I ran the check against the ARTIFACT'S OWN oracle, sprs_core._fp64_add_bits, rather than a fresh transcription of the RTL, so the result additionally proves the oracle inherits the defect -- which means the reproducibility appendix's boast at main.tex:3084-3086 ('Python bit-exact FADD mirror ... identical output to RTL on ~10^6 randomised inputs') is true and evidentially empty, and needs one qualifying clause. Unreachability by the campaign confirmed at src/sprs_core.py:5366-5368: the leaf generator is strictly positive for every index, so s_a == s_b on every FADD in all 2,822 runs and effective_sub is never asserted. Verdict: CONFIRMED_NARROWER. Action: MUST DISCLOSE (a fourth deviation in Sec.3.6 plus one clause in app:repro), not MUST FIX, because no reported number changes and Claim 1 is about agreement rather than accuracy.
headline: Sixteen docket issues, and the theme's own framing needs correcting in both directions. Nine are CONFIRMED, seven CONFIRMED_NARROWER, and among six extended findings two are REFUTED. The VC verdict is worse than the docket says and the deadlock verdict is better. Worse: the discipline is not merely unimplemented -- I built the channel-dependency graph from the compiler's own emitted routing tables and it is CYCLIC on all four ring instances (cycle length = G) and all five torus instances (length 6 to 32), so every one of Sec.4.9's five clauses is false: the routing is greedy minimal, not dimension-ordered (sprs_core.py:667-686); no packet ever leaves VC0 (btree_fsm_fast.sv:629); the CDG is not acyclic; C-route is not discharged; and validate_routing.py, the 30-line checker cited to verify it, is not in the artifact -- nor are tb/sva/tb_sva_e2e.sv or validate_abi.py, which together carry every dynamic-assertion claim in Sec.3.8. The router could not implement the discipline in any case, because its egress FIFO is shared across VCs (noc_router.sv:142-143). Better: the theme's hypothesis that this explains the 21 watchdog timeouts is REFUTED -- at least 10 of the 21 are on hypercube and fat-tree instances whose CDGs I computed to be acyclic, and T01 showed the failures cluster by S2 algorithm, not topology. Three more narrowings matter as much as the confirmations. The credit mis-sizing (D067) cannot corrupt a result: a dropped packet leaves a scoreboard bit clear forever, so it can only produce a watchdog fail-stop, which means zero drops occurred in any of the 2,822 passing runs -- a free argument that voids the reviewer's 'affects all cycle counts'. The fat-tree port overflow (D063) is silently discarded by the RTL and costs nothing: I rebuilt the fabric the hardware actually installs and routed up to 1,599 leaf-to-leaf pairs per instance through the emitted tables with zero dead ports and zero non-terminating paths; only surplus core switches are orphaned, and the declared radix is 100% wired on every instance, so Table I and the O(P^2) crossbar argument survive intact. The credit-counter overflow (D070) is unreachable for exactly the reason the VC finding identifies. Two things are worse than the reviewers claimed. maxp_mod_fat is not 'resource-limited' and not merely 'unbuildable': I emulated the 12-bit adjacency truncation exactly as noc_system.sv applies it and found that ZERO of the 8,223 installed links match the intended topology and ZERO of 900 sampled leaf-to-leaf routes deliver -- the instance would have elaborated, run, and hung, so L0's explanation is false and 58.9 core-hours were spent on a configuration that could never settle. And the artifact shows a systematic pattern -- VC1 dead, CN link 1 dead, k/2-1 core switches dead, noc_link.sv compiled but never instantiated, six unreferenced parameters including two conflicting MAX_PORTS -- in which every latent defect this theme found lives in the unused half of a parameter the campaign exercised at one point. Finally, the paper twice UNDERSTATES itself: eleven lines at main.tex:1276-1287 argue for value-agnostic VC steering that the constant VC bit makes trivially true, and the fat-tree Omega ratios are computed against a more capable network than the one simulated, so they are conservative. The net of all sixteen issues plus six extensions is NEGATIVE billed pages: one paragraph deleted, one compressed, and roughly a dozen one-line corrections, with the only irreducible cost being a four-sentence honest restatement of C-route.
correct_restatement: For Sec.4.9, replacing the DOR/VC-escape paragraph and its L-item: 'The fabric instantiates NUM_VCS = 2 virtual channels per input port and steers on packet bit [64]. The present compiler emits every packet on VC0 and does not assign virtual channels, and the routing tables it emits are minimal-distance rather than dimension-ordered; on ring and torus instances the resulting channel-dependency graph contains cycles. C-route is therefore an assumption of Claim 1 that the compiler does not discharge, not a property we establish. Deadlock is possible in principle and the fabric converts it into a fail-stop: a stalled processing element that does not retire for WATCHDOG_MAX = 20,000 cycles raises P_ERROR with a recorded error_pc and error_state. We observed 21 such fail-stops across the 2,844 attempted configurations and no run in the campaign produced a finite root differing from the canonical one. A compiler-side dimension-ordered pass with a VC-escape assignment, and a per-VC egress buffer to make the escape channel real, are the two changes a production deployment would need.' For L0, replacing the resource explanation: 'maxp_mod_fat (N=8192, G=4096, fat-tree) instantiates 4,192 routers, but the adjacency-configuration interface carries a 12-bit router id (noc_system.sv:67-70) with 12'hFFF taken as the disconnected sentinel, so the addressable range is 0..4,094 and the 96 routers above it alias onto routers 0..95. The emitted configuration therefore does not describe the intended topology and the instance cannot settle regardless of wall-clock; the five attempts that consumed 58.9 core-hours were bounded by this, not by the 28,800 s cap. MAX_ROUTERS in noc_pkg.sv is vestigial and enforces nothing, as is MAX_PORTS. The compiler still produces an ABI-compliant image for the instance, and its software oracle agrees with the N=8192 root reported by the two validated configurations at that leaf count.' For Sec.3.6, adding a fourth deviation: 'Fourth, effective subtraction does not borrow the alignment tail recorded in the sticky bit and then applies the addition rounding rule, so a sum of opposite-signed operands whose exponents differ by 5 to 52 binades is high by one ulp about half the time, and by one ulp always at a difference of exactly 53. The campaign cannot detect this: its leaf generator is strictly positive, so no FADD in any of the 2,822 runs takes the subtraction path, and the Python oracle is a mirror of the same RTL. No result reported here is affected, and a user reducing mixed-sign data would inherit a reduction that is deterministic but not the IEEE-correct one.'
